items.test_passage: AIRTBench, an AI red teaming benchmark for evaluating language models’ ability to autonomously discover and exploit Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML) security vulnerabilities.
items.runner_passage: dreadnode, Canada dreadnode, USA dreadnode, USA dreadnode, USA (all four authors; tested models are from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, Meta, DeepSeek, Alibaba)
items.pass_passage: No pass mark or threshold applied to the results; success rates only.
items.outside_passage: We open-sourced our evaluation tools and data to support community-driven development and position AIRTBench as a standard for red teaming LLMs.
items.models: claude-3-7-sonnet, gemini-2.5-pro/flash/1.5/2.0, gpt-4.5-preview, gpt-4o, llama-3.3-70b, llama-4-scout, DeepSeek-R1 and others, via public APIs (hosted by makers or third-party hosts: public API and open weights)

pairs.quote: The benchmark operates in realistic black-box scenarios where agents lack access to underlying system architecture, mirroring authentic adversarial conditions.

items.note: The paper is a black-box benchmark; it makes no comparison with code-analysis evaluations and reports no transfer result. gpt-4.5-preview was deprecated by OpenAI during the study (stated in the paper).

items.route: direct curl arxiv.org/pdf/2505.23836 + pdftotext, full text
items.test_passage: We investigate whether frontier language models can accurately classify transcripts based on whether they originate from evaluations or real-world deployment, a capability we call evaluation awareness.
items.runner_passage: Authors at MATS and Apollo Research; none at the developers of the nine models tested (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google).
items.pass_passage: No pass mark applied; AUC compared with a human baseline only.
items.outside_passage: Dataset and code are available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/jjpn2/eval_awareness and https://github.com/jjpn97/eval_awareness.
items.models: Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, GPT-4o, o4-mini

pairs.quote: Frontier models clearly demonstrate above-random evaluation awareness (Gemini-2.5-Pro reaches an AUC of 0.83), but do not yet surpass our simple human baseline (AUC of 0.92).

items.note: The paper supports the third-party experiment half of the sentence; it does not itself cover pre-deployment testing by developers.

items.route: direct curl arxiv.org/pdf/2408.15221 + pdftotext, full text
items.test_passage: commissioning expert human red teamers with access to a multi-turn LLM chat interface – mirroring the user experience on model interfaces such as ChatGPT.
items.runner_passage: 1 Scale AI, 2 UC Berkeley (defended models are Llama-3-8B-Instruct-based; CYGNET by Gray Swan; none of the authors works for those developers)
items.pass_passage: No pass mark; attack success rates are reported.
items.outside_passage: We publicly release MHJ alongside a compendium of jailbreak tactics
items.models: Defenses RR, LAT, DERTA (open source) on llama-3-8b-instruct; CYGNET (closed source, reached through the Gray Swan AI API); GPT-4o as harm classifier

pairs.quote: Post-experimentation, we found 91.62% of successful HarmBench submissions and 85.7% of successful WMDP-Bio submissions required more than one turn of conversation to reach a successful jailbreak.

items.note: Supports that multi-turn attacks outperform single-turn automated ones, but the comparison also differs in attacker (human vs automated), as the paper itself says; red team composition and tools are not varied in the paper. MHJ release removes sensitive items (Section 7).

items.test_passage: we run three experiments on an LLM trained to be helpful, honest, and harmless with Constitutional AI.
items.runner_passage: All authors list Anthropic; the model tested is Anthropic's own ("Correspondence to: esin at anthropic dot com").
items.outside_passage: The model is not named: "We study a decoder-only transformer model fine-tuned with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) [18, 76] and Constitutional AI (CAI)"; dataset released.

pairs.quote: such applications may require language models to make subjective judgments that could vary significantly across different social groups

items.note: Cited for actions whose helpfulness or harmfulness is a matter of opinion; the paper concerns whose opinions responses resemble, not helpfulness or harmfulness as such.
